name: Screen Pap tests and other cytology in the community laboratory
summary: Cervical screening Pap tests arrive as liquid-based vials, are made into thin-layer slides by laboratory assistants and screened under the microscope by cytotechnologists, one slide at a time within a daily workload limit. Negative cases, about nine in ten, are rescreened at random by a second cytotechnologist and signed out by cytotechnologists; abnormal, unsatisfactory and all non-gynaecologic cases are marked and passed to a pathologist. The work is slow because screening is manual and capped per person, and most elapsed time is cases waiting in the screening queue; errors are mostly missed abnormal cells, which rescreening and look-backs are designed to catch.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company with cytology at its main laboratories, liquid-based processors, automated staining and manual screening by cytotechnologists.
baseline.notes: About 32,000 cytology cases a month, about 96% gynaecologic. Cervical screening in Ontario was cytology-based in this period; HPV primary screening began in 2025.

trigger: An accessioned cytology specimen (usually a liquid-based Pap vial) reaches the cytology laboratory.
end_state: A negative report is signed out by a cytotechnologist and the slide filed, or the case is marked and delivered to a pathologist, or the specimen is rejected for unresolved identification.

volume.seasonality: Steady on weekdays; lower in summer and December holiday periods when clinics see fewer screening patients.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate.

The company posts a Clinical Laboratory Assistant role in cytology at $22.00 to $24.50 an hour (2026), times 1.35 gives about $30 to $33; the organisation file has no cytology assistant role, so this role is added. FTE derived from minutes times volume. Loaded cost is hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Duties from the company cytotechnologist posting; FTE derived from screening minutes times volume within the 40 headcount. Loaded cost is hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

roles.title: Charge technologist
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: A senior cytotechnologist acting as charge technologist assigns work and reviews equivocal slides; FTE derived. Loaded cost is hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Anatomic pathology case management with dictation and synoptic reporting
Liquid-based cytology processors and slide imaging
Slide and residual vial storage and filing

steps.name: Receive vials and check labels against the LIS
steps.description: The cytology laboratory assistant takes the accessioned liquid-based vials and other cytology specimens from processing, scans each one, checks the two patient identifiers on the vial against the requisition and the LIS order, and sorts gynaecologic vials from non-gynaecologic specimens.

control.basis: Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice: two-identifier specimen labelling and acceptance

evidence.note: Labelling, sample preparation and demographic checks are listed duties; shares are estimates (about 4% non-gynaecologic).

steps.name: Hold the case and contact the clinic
steps.description: The laboratory assistant records the discrepancy, puts the case on hold in the LIS and phones or faxes the clinic to confirm the patient's identity or request a corrected requisition.

control.basis: Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice: specimens with unresolved identification are not tested

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Clinic confirms identity or sends a corrected requisition
steps.description: The clinic replies by fax or phone with the confirmed identity or a corrected requisition; if identity cannot be confirmed the vial is rejected and the clinic is told to recollect.

evidence.note: Response times and rejection share are estimates.

steps.name: Load vials on the liquid-based processor
steps.description: The laboratory assistant loads gynaecologic vials into the liquid-based cytology processor in batches; the processor mixes each vial, collects cells on a filter and transfers a thin layer to a barcoded slide, which drops into fixative.

error.defect_description: Slide made from the wrong vial or vial not processed.

evidence.note: Liquid-based collection is over 90% of Pap tests in the US and sample preparation is a cytology assistant duty; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Processor run, Papanicolaou stain and coverslip
steps.description: The processor finishes the batch and the slides go through the automated Papanicolaou stainer and coverslipper; nobody works on the case while the instruments run.

evidence.note: Batch and stain run times are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare non-gynaecologic slides
steps.description: For urine, sputum and fluid specimens the laboratory assistant concentrates the cells by cytospin or liquid-based preparation, stains the slides, matches them to the case and places them on the non-gynaecologic screening tray.

error.defect_description: Poor cellularity from a preparation error.

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Match slides to cases and assemble screening trays
steps.description: The laboratory assistant checks each slide label against the vial and the case in the anatomic pathology system, attaches the patient's prior cytology and histology results from the LIS, and builds screening trays.

control.basis: Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice: slide identification at each handoff

evidence.note: Verifying patient demographics is a listed duty; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Assign trays within screening workload limits
steps.description: The charge cytotechnologist assigns trays to each cytotechnologist's worklist so that no one exceeds their individual daily slide limit, and prioritises cases with a history of abnormal results or past their turnaround target.

control.basis: Daily screening workload limit per cytotechnologist set from past performance and reassessed every six months (Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice)

evidence.note: Individual workload limits, a 100-slide absolute maximum and six-monthly reassessment are described; minutes per case are estimates.

steps.name: Screen a gynaecologic slide
steps.description: The cytotechnologist screens the whole slide under the microscope, assesses specimen adequacy, marks any abnormal cells with ink dots and records a Bethesda interpretation, counting the slide toward the daily workload limit.

error.defect_description: Abnormal cells missed in primary screening (false negative).

control.basis: Daily screening workload limit (Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice; 100 slides in 24 hours in the US rule)

next.condition: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy

evidence.note: Abnormal share from 2006 CAP medians (ASC-US 4.3%, LSIL 2.9% liquid-based, HSIL 0.5%, ASC-H about 0.2%, AGC about 0.3%) plus 1.1% unsatisfactory for ThinPrep; about 4.8 minutes per slide follows from 100 slides in 8 hours with 6.5 to 7 hours of screening. The queue wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reprocess an unsatisfactory or obscured slide
steps.description: For a bloody or poorly cellular slide the laboratory assistant treats the residual vial (for example with an acetic acid wash) and makes and stains a new slide, which returns to the cytotechnologist.

evidence.note: Common liquid-based practice; share and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Select negative cases for rescreening
steps.description: The anatomic pathology system selects at least 10% of negative gynaecologic cases at random, plus cases from patients at higher risk, for rescreening by a second cytotechnologist before the result is reported.

control.basis: Rescreen of at least 10% of negative gynaecologic cases, including high-risk patients, before reporting (Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice)

evidence.note: At least 10% random plus high-risk; 12% total selected is an estimate.

steps.name: Rescreen a negative slide
steps.description: A second cytotechnologist rescreens the selected negative slide, records agreement or the abnormality found, and sends any discrepancy for senior review.

control.basis: Rescreen of negative cases before reporting (Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice)

evidence.note: Rescreening is described; the discrepancy share and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Sign out the negative report
steps.description: The cytotechnologist checks the demographics, adequacy statement and the screening-program recommendation comment, then releases the negative report from the anatomic pathology system to the LIS for delivery.

error.defect_description: Wrong recommendation comment or demographic error.

control.basis: Laboratory policy under accreditation: negative gynaecologic cases may be released by a registered cytotechnologist (Medical Laboratory Technology Act, 1991 scope); abnormal cases require a pathologist

evidence.note: Pathologist confirmation is required for abnormal slides and the MLT scope covers evaluating results; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: File slides and keep vials for the retention period
steps.description: The laboratory assistant files the signed-out slides in numbered boxes for long-term retention and keeps the residual vials in dated racks for the weeks set by policy so add-on tests remain possible.

control.basis: Retention of cytology slides and records so they are retrievable on request (Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice)

evidence.note: Slide retention and specimen storage are described; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Senior cytotechnologist reviews an equivocal or discrepant slide
steps.description: The charge cytotechnologist reviews the dotted areas and the whole slide where needed, decides whether the case is negative or needs the pathologist, and records the outcome for the rescreen statistics.

evidence.note: Common practice; shares and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Screen a non-gynaecologic slide
steps.description: The cytotechnologist screens the urine, sputum or fluid slides, marks atypical or malignant cells and records a preliminary interpretation; all non-gynaecologic cases go to the pathologist.

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Mark cells and prepare the case for the pathologist
steps.description: The cytotechnologist confirms the ink dots, enters the preliminary Bethesda or descriptive interpretation, pulls the patient's prior cytology and biopsy results, and places the case in the pathologist's queue.

control.basis: A pathologist confirms every gynaecologic slide with reactive, atypical, premalignant or malignant changes (Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice)

next.condition: new high-grade lesion with prior negative slides on file

evidence.note: Pathologist confirmation of abnormal slides is described; minutes and look-back share are estimates.

steps.name: Pull prior negative slides for a look-back
steps.description: For a new high-grade lesion the cytotechnologist retrieves the patient's negative slides from the past five years from the file and rescreens them so the pathologist can review any discrepancy with the current case.

control.basis: Five-year look-back of prior negative slides for a new high-grade lesion (Accreditation cytology requirements under ISO 15189 (IQMH in Ontario, MANQAP in Manitoba); the US rule 42 CFR 493.1274 describes the same practice)

evidence.note: The five-year look-back is stated; share and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Deliver the case to the pathologist
steps.description: The laboratory assistant collects the referred slides with their worksheets and delivers the trays to the pathologists' offices on the scheduled runs, scanning the handoff in the anatomic pathology system.

evidence.note: Delivery runs are common practice; times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Identification discrepancy
exceptions.description: Vial and requisition do not match; the case waits for the clinic and a quarter are rejected.

exceptions.name: Reprocessed slide
exceptions.description: Bloody or poorly cellular slides are reprocessed from the residual vial and screened again.

exceptions.name: Abnormal or unsatisfactory case
exceptions.description: Marked and sent to the pathologist.

exceptions.name: Rescreen discrepancy
exceptions.description: The rescreen finds an abnormality missed in primary screening; senior review and pathologist referral follow.

exceptions.name: Five-year look-back
exceptions.description: Prior negative slides are rescreened for a new high-grade lesion.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt in cytology to sign-out or referral
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for a high-volume Canadian community cytology laboratory in 2019-2022

evidence.note: No opened source gives community Pap turnaround for the period; the estimate assumes about a week of screening queue, longer during pandemic backlogs.

pain_points.description: Manual screening is capped per person, so cytotechnologist availability sets turnaround and backlogs build quickly when staff are short.

evidence.note: Workload caps and the loss of accuracy above about 100 slides a day are described.

pain_points.description: Screening accuracy falls when workload rises or late in the day, and missed abnormal cells are found only by rescreening or later biopsies.

evidence.note: Elsheikh et al.: performance fell above 100 slides a day and in afternoon screening.

pain_points.description: Identification discrepancies between vial and requisition hold cases for days while clinics respond.

evidence.note: Common practice.

pain_points.description: Most hands-on effort goes to the nine in ten slides that are negative.

evidence.note: About 9% abnormal or unsatisfactory.

sources.title: 42 CFR 493.1274 Standard: Cytology
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: US rule used as a reference for common practice: review of at least 10% of negative gynaecologic cases, randomly selected and including high-risk patients, before reporting; maximum 100 slides per person per 24 hours, not a performance target, individual limits reassessed every 6 months; a pathologist confirms every gynaecologic slide with reactive, atypical, premalignant or malignant changes; five-year look-back of prior negatives for a new HSIL or cancer; comparison of HSIL cytology with histology; annual statistical evaluation; slides retained and retrievable.

sources.title: Cytology screening limits, by the numbers (Paxton)
sources.supports: CLIA limit of 100 slides in an eight-hour day; imaging-assisted systems 200 (ThinPrep) or 170 (FocalPoint) slides a day; full-day cytotechnologists screen about 6.5 to 7 hours; imaging raises productivity 30 to 50%; 95 to 99% of cytotechnologists are set at the maximum limit; liquid-based collection is over 90% of US Pap tests; negative cases require a 10% rescreen; five-year look-back for new high-grade dysplasia.

sources.title: Imaging systems, workload limits, and screening accuracy (Lane)
sources.supports: ThinPrep imager presents 22 fields of view per slide; in Elsheikh et al. 2010 workloads rose from 87 to 118 slides a day and above 100 slides a day screening performance fell (fewer manual reviews, lower detection, higher false-negative fraction).

assumptions: The organisation file's cytology unit holds only cytotechnologists (40). Slide preparation, matching, filing and delivery are given to a cytology laboratory assistant role added with not_in_org_file (about 9 FTE), because the company posts such a role; the organisation file should add it.

Abnormal and unsatisfactory gynaecologic cases (about 9.1%) and all non-gynaecologic cases (about 4%) go to the pathologist, as the process map describes. This sends about 4,100 cases a month to pathology sign-out, slightly more than the process map's 16,000 sign-out volume implies when added to 13,000 surgical cases.
Pathologist review of referred cytology is documented in the pathology sign-out workflow, so the pathologist role listed in the process map has no step here.
Primary screening is manual at about 5.5 minutes a slide; imaging-assisted screening, which raises productivity 30 to 50%, is not assumed for the company in this period.

Workload limits, rescreening and look-backs follow Canadian accreditation practice; the US CLIA rule is cited only as a public statement of the same requirements. The Canadian maximum daily slide count was not confirmed from an opened source.
The screening queue (1 to 7 days, mode 3) is the author's estimate; pandemic backlogs in 2020 and 2021 would push it higher.
HPV testing was not part of routine Ontario screening in 2019-2022 and is not modelled.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (hourly wage times 1.35) except the added cytology assistant.
